question: A 32-year-old woman asks for preconceptional advice. The patient reports that she underwent cervical conization due to a high-grade intraepithelial lesion (H-SIL) and that she subsequently suffered three miscarriages between 20 and 22 weeks of gestation. He does not have living children. On all three occasions he went to the Emergency Department with a sensation of weight in the hypogastrium and there it was found that he arrived with a dilatation of 8 cm and with prominent amniotic membranes. I had never felt contractions. What advice would you give for the next pregnancy?

options.opa: I would recommend prophylaxis with atosiban orally throughout the pregnancy.
options.opb: It would offer lung maturation with corticosteroids from 19-20 weeks of gestation.
options.opc: I would recommend performing a cervical cerclage programmed from the 14th week of gestation.
options.opd: I would advise you not to try more pregnancies because of the high risk of recurrence.
options.ope: I would recommend resorting to assisted reproduction techniques.
